Leiden returns the two clusters as communities, each one connected, drawn as tinted regions in the accent color and teal. The card lists community 0 as A, B, C and community 1 as D, E, F, G." width="100%"} Leiden (Traag, Waltman & van Eck, 2019) finds a partition with high modularity, like Louvain, and fixes Louvain's main flaw: Louvain can produce communities that are internally disconnected, or held together by a single node. Leiden adds a refinement step between Louvain's local moving and aggregation phases, which only ever merges nodes into well-connected subsets, so **every community it returns is connected**. It also tends to reach higher modularity, and does so quickly, which makes it the usual recommendation over Louvain today. The algorithm is repeated, each run starting from the previous partition, until the quality stops improving. Edge weights are used on weighted graphs (`Graph(weighted=True)`). Leiden can optimize either of two qualities, chosen with `objective=`: - `"modularity"` (default): the usual modularity (see `modularity()`), which compares each community against a random graph with the same degrees. - `"cpm"`: the Constant Potts Model (see `constant_potts_model()`), which rewards edges inside communities and charges `resolution` for every pair of nodes placed together. Here `resolution` is a density threshold: communities end up with an internal edge density above it and are linked to each other with a density below it. CPM has no resolution limit, so small, dense groups are found even in a very large graph, but `resolution` must be set to suit the graph. On an unweighted graph, values between `0` and `1` make sense (the graph's density is a natural starting point); at `1` or above, no merge pays off and every node stays in a community of its own. NetworkX's `community.leiden_communities()` defaults to `"cpm"`; pass `objective="cpm"` to match it. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [resolution]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[1.0]{.fl}]{.doc-parameter-default} : The resolution parameter of the objective. With modularity, values above `1.0` produce more, smaller communities and values below `1.0` fewer, larger ones. With CPM, it is the density threshold described above (larger values give smaller, denser communities). Default is `1.0`. [seed]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Random seed. The algorithm visits nodes in random order, so different seeds can give (usually slightly) different partitions. Set it for reproducible results. [objective]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [["modularity"]{.st}]{.doc-parameter-default} : The quality to maximize: `"modularity"` (default) or `"cpm"`. [theta]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[0.01]{.fl}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Randomness of the refinement step. A refined subset is chosen with probability proportional to `exp(gain / theta)`, so small values almost always take the best merge and larger ones explore more. Must be positive. Default is `0.01`, the value Traag et al. recommend. [attr_name]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Name of the node attribute to store community labels in. If `None` (default), uses `"cmty_leiden"`. [return_dict]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True`, returns a dictionary instead of self. If `False` (default), stores the community labels as a node attribute and returns self for chaining. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Union[dict[int, int], Graph]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `return_dict=` is `True`: a dictionary mapping node IDs to community labels (`0`, `1`, ..., numbered in order of the lowest node ID in each). If `return_dict=` is `False` (default): returns self. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If the graph is directed, `objective=` is not `"modularity"` or `"cpm"`, or `theta=` is not positive. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Two triangles joined by a bridge split into their natural communities: ::: {#fa26e270 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_nodes(["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]) .add_edges([("A", "B"), ("B", "C"), ("C", "A"), ("C", "D"), ("D", "E"), ("E", "F"), ("F", "D")]) ) communities = graph.cmty_leiden(seed=1, return_dict=True) {graph.get_label_from_id(n): c for n, c in sorted(communities.items())} ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` {'A': 0, 'B': 0, 'C': 0, 'D': 1, 'E': 1, 'F': 1} ``` ::: ::: On Zachary's karate club, Leiden reaches the best modularity known for the network: ::: {#cd58f3b2 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} karate = ec.karate_club() karate.cmty_leiden(seed=1) labels = karate.get_node_attrs("cmty_leiden") round(karate.modularity("cmty_leiden"), 4), len(set(labels.values())) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` (0.4198, 4) ``` ::: ::: With `objective="cpm"`, `resolution` sets the density a community must exceed. A low threshold keeps the two factions of the karate club; a higher one breaks them into smaller, denser groups: ::: {#33871274 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} [ len(set(karate.cmty_leiden(objective="cpm", resolution=r, seed=1, return_dict=True).values())) for r in [0.05, 0.2, 0.5] ] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` [2, 7, 19] ``` ::: :::
